title: SandboxAQ and Northrop Grumman Flight-Test AQNav Quantum Navigation on Attritable Drone - Quantum Computing Report
gist: SandboxAQ flight-tested its AQNav magnetic navigation system on Northrop Grumman's Lumberjack attritable one-way-attack drone, the first reported MagNav deployment on an expendable UAS, extending a 450+ flight-hour track record into low-cost, mass-manufacturable defense platforms for GPS-denied navigation.

insights.claim: SandboxAQ completed a successful flight-test of its AQNav magnetic navigation (MagNav) system integrated onto Northrop Grumman's Lumberjack, a Group 3 one-way-attack attritable Unmanned Aircraft System, marking the first reported MagNav payload flight-test on an expendable attritable drone platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Expands quantum-sensing navigation's addressable market from exquisite manned/large platforms into the high-volume, low-cost expendable drone category central to modern attritable warfare.
insights.quote: the first reported operational flight-test of a MagNav payload deployed on an expendable, attritable drone platform
insights.locator: AI and quantum technology enterprise SandboxAQ

insights.claim: The test also marked the first reported pairing of magnetic anomaly navigation with visual navigation sensors on a one-way attack drone system.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sensor-fusion (magnetic plus visual) on a low-cost strike drone is a differentiator versus single-sensor Alt-PNT approaches and could become a template other attritable-drone programs adopt.
insights.locator: as well as the first reported pairing of magnetic anomaly navigation

insights.claim: AQNav's hardware-agnostic, software-first architecture uses Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) and physics-based geomagnetic anomaly maps to filter out electromagnetic interference from onboard motors and electronics in real time, running on the drone's existing compute without added specialized processing hardware, with installation and software integration completed in under one hour.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sub-one-hour integration with no new hardware lowers the switching cost for defense primes to retrofit existing drone fleets with GPS-denied navigation, a key factor for rapid scale-up.
insights.quote: engineers completed system installation and software integration in under one hour
insights.locator: The flight-test validated SandboxAQ's new hardware-agnostic

insights.claim: The AQNav program builds on SandboxAQ's participation in the Defense Innovation Unit's Transition of Quantum Sensing (TQS) program and NATO's DIANA cohort, both of which evaluate quantum magnetometry and MagNav payloads for unjammable military autonomy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Inclusion in both a US DoD innovation pipeline (DIU) and a NATO innovation accelerator (DIANA) signals a funded, allied-government path toward eventual programs of record.
insights.locator: The initiative builds on SandboxAQ's participation

insights.claim: SandboxAQ has accumulated over 450 flight-test hours for AQNav across heavy military transports (C-17 Globemaster III, C-130J Super Hercules) and commercial airframes, and is now extending the platform into attritable Group 3 UAS to pursue low-cost, mass-manufacturable defense systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A track record spanning large manned transports down to small expendable drones de-risks AQNav as a multi-platform navigation standard rather than a single-program demo.
insights.quote: With over 450 flight-test hours accumulated across heavy military transports
insights.locator: The initiative builds on SandboxAQ's participation
